text:
juan: Heads-up — saw a perf regression on the new kernel selector for long-context jobs (16k tokens). latency jumped ~25% on the FlashA variant we default to. nsys snapshot attached in the ticket but quick paste below.

mira: ugh, can you paste the hot stacks? is it memcopy or compute?

juan: hotspot looks like shared-memory spills + multiple memcpy HtoD in pipeline stage 2. nsys top:
```
GPU Activity: 98% cycles
DRAM throughput: 530 GB/s (device peak 900 GB/s)
SharedMem throughput spike correlated with attention kernel
Kernel: flash_attn_v2_tile32  (avg)  62ms
Kernel: flash_attn_fused  (avg)  48ms
```
memory-bound. also saw bank-conflict warnings when we ran with shmem tile=128.

sam: interesting — so our selector picked the tiling that maximizes compute reuse but kills bandwidth. looks like the heuristics favored fewer kernel launches over memory locality.

anya: perf-bot shows increase in p50 and p99 for the 16k benchmark after the selector change on the canary cluster:
`perf-bot: 16k-lc | p50 +22% | p99 +18% | tokens/s -19%`

juan: exact. hypothesis: the chosen FlashA tile size increases shared-memory footprint per CTA forcing more global loads and bank conflicts for large KV shapes. the old fused path had smaller per-thread state and better coalescing.

mira: options: 1) tweak selector to prefer fused-attn when seq_len >= 8k (simple fix), 2) add an occupancy floor — if shmem per-CTA > X, skip variant, 3) try pipeline reordering to reduce HtoD memcopies.

sam: also consider lowering tile width and increasing pipeline depth. that reduces per-CTA shmem but may increase launches. need to benchmark kernel launch overhead vs bandwidth.

juan: I ran a quick micro-benchmark switching tile=64 vs tile=128 on the same 16k model:
```
tile=128: avg kernel 62ms, dram 530 GB/s, bank-conflict=high
tile=64 : avg kernel 50ms, dram 410 GB/s, bank-conflict=low
fused   : avg kernel 48ms, dram 380 GB/s
```
So smaller tile reduced bandwidth and conflicts — despite more launches it's faster.

anya: nice. can we codify that: if estimated dram > 0.6 * peak, prefer smaller tile or fused? We have a rack-level value for peak per device.

perf-bot: autotune sweep queued: tag=attn-tiling-176789 | variants=tile{32,48,64,96,128} | seq={4k,8k,16k} | rep=5

mira: also add a KV-cache check: when KV cache hits > 70% reuse, the page layout changes — selector must account for effective working set, not just seq_len. otherwise we mis-predict live memory.

sam: agree. next steps:
- juan run the autotune sweep and push results to /perf/artifacts/attn-tiling-176789 (csv + nsys). (owner: juan)
- mira update selector heuristics PR draft to add occupancy & dram threshold rules (owner: mira)
- sam validate fallback to fused-attn on canary (owner: sam)
- anya add a regression gate for 16k synthetic tests in CI (owner: anya)

juan: starting sweep now. will ping when artifacts uploaded. thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: thanks — also throw in a quick per-block shared-memory bank-access histogram if possible, that's been helpful before.

anya: noted. tagging infra to keep canary stable: @eng-oncall please note the scheduled autotune burst on canary cluster — will be low-impact but spikes possible.

perf-bot: note: autotune run scheduled at 1767890800.

juan: will close loop when results land.
